speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know that many households are feeling the pressure of higher living costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fortunately, we had some unexpected revenue upside from our strong economic rebound in the preceding two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this is why the Government was able to enhance its assistance measures to relieve the burden on households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Growth in the major economies on the whole is expected to remain resilient.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Wars are raging in Europe and the Middle East.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These conflicts can escalate dangerously, leading to disruptions in global energy markets and supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Global inflationary pressures are expected to recede further.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This may provide some room for the major central banks to adopt more accommodative stances, which may ease financial conditions and support demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The global electronics industry is expected to recover.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will bolster the growth of many regional economies, including our key trading partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, Asia continues to be a key driver of global growth, with a wider spread of opportunities across the region – not just in China, but also in India and many parts of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the whole, we are cautiously optimistic that 2024 will be a better year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is considerable uncertainty in the outlook and the risks are tilted to the downside.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The post-Cold War era that began in the early 1990s and fostered three decades of peace and stability is over.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are now in a new era of conflict and confrontation, and there is no turning back.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What can we expect in this new world?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We already see a growing zone of impunity involving armed conflict and terrorism that cannot be easily resolved by the global community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because the major powers are prioritising national security over economic interdependence, and traditional modes of cooperation are breaking down.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because there will be diminished willingness and capacity to tackle global issues, be it responding to future pandemics or tackling climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For some time to come, Singapore will have to operate in an external environment that will be less stable and favourable to our security and prosperity than the preceding three decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we embarked on the Forward Singapore exercise – to refresh our social compact to keep our society strong and united, and to set out a roadmap for our way forward in this very troubled world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through Forward Singapore, we aim to give more assurance to help Singaporeans navigate the uncertainties in today’s world; strengthen our sense of cohesion and solidarity; and keep our society together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For as one united people, we can overcome all odds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can turn every challenge into opportunity and every vulnerability into strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can build a nation that is vibrant and inclusive, fair and thriving, resilient and united.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have an ambitious agenda to achieve these shared goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have major plans to unfold over the coming years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others will require more time to study or to work out the implementation details.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we will roll out the first instalment of our Forward Singapore programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Budget 2024 is therefore about taking concrete steps to build our shared future together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will: (a) tackle immediate challenges for households and businesses; (b) pursue better growth and jobs, and equip our workers for life; (c) create more paths for equality and mobility; (d) provide more assurance for families and seniors; (e) and ultimately, forge a stronger and more united nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will touch on each of these in turn in the rest of my speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have enjoyed low inflation in Singapore for more than a decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But inflation rose sharply in 2022, following the outbreak of the war in Ukraine, which led to significant increases in global energy and food prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite the unprecedented surge in prices, we had good economic growth in 2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, incomes that year rose faster than inflation and Singaporeans were better off, in real terms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While we expect the situation to improve this year, there are uncertainties in the outlook, as I mentioned just now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in this Budget, I will do more to support households and further enhance the Assurance Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The first $300 will be disbursed in end-June this year, and the remaining $300 will be disbursed in January next year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be extended to adult Singaporeans with Assessable Income of up to $100,000, and who do not own more than one property.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, I will provide additional one-off U-Save rebates to help HDB households cope with increases in their utility bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will cover about four months of utility bills for those living in 3- and 4- room flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fourth, I will provide an additional one-off Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) Rebate for HDB flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together with the regular S&CC rebates, eligible Housing and Development Board (HDB) households will receive up to four months of such rebates in FY2024.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have designed the Assurance Package so that lower-income families get more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also ensured that larger households, particularly those with seniors and children, get more support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This comprises cash, MediSave top-ups, U-Save and S&CC rebates, and CDC Vouchers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A middle-income household of four, with two young children, will receive about $3,000 in benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A middle-income household with six persons – a larger family – including two seniors and two young children, will receive about $8,000 in benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This delivers on our commitment to permanently defray GST expenses for lower- and middle-income households, through the GST Voucher scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Businesses also need help to manage rising costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not all companies are profitable, and some may not benefit from such a rebate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I will provide a minimum benefit of $2,000 in cash payouts for companies that employed at least one local employee in 2023.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I will enhance the Enterprise Financing Scheme, which helps Singapore enterprises with their financing needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The maximum working capital loan quantum will be permanently raised to $500,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also extend until 31 March 2025 the enhanced maximum trade loan quantum, as well as the Government’s risk sharing of project loans to support domestic construction projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, I will extend the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit by a year to 30 June 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Credit provides additional support for eligible employers to cover their out-of-pocket expenses when they embark on workforce and business transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this extension, employers will have another year to claim any unused credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The measures in this Enterprise Support Package are tilted towards firms that make the effort to restructure and transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I encourage all firms to make full use of these schemes, so that they can thrive and succeed, amidst a more challenging operating environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The enhanced Assurance Package and the Enterprise Support Package will provide some near-term relief to Singaporean households and firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are needed during this difficult period when inflation, while moderating, remains on the high side.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the longer term, the best way to deal with inflation is to ensure that our firms and workers are more productive, and that real incomes continue to rise sustainably.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our key priority is to ensure a strong, innovative and vibrant economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is absolutely essential to secure good jobs and better lives for all Singaporeans, and on a sustained basis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since our early days of independence, we have been able to defy the odds and consistently achieve good economic performance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we cannot afford to be complacent, especially in a more complex and volatile external environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In past years, some had suggested that Singapore should slow down, do not have to grow so quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, that happened last year – our economy grew by just about 1%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if we were to experience similarly slow growth for several years in a row, we will be in trouble.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have no chance of improving our collective wellbeing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will not be able to afford the social services we need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And in the end, lower-income workers and families will be hit the hardest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We therefore make no apology for pursuing growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be clear, we are not going for growth at all costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a limit to how fast we can grow due to the tighter constraints we face in land, labour and carbon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But by focusing on productivity and innovation, we can push the frontier and grow at an average of about 2% to 3% each year over the next decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is an ambitious goal given our stage of economic development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must aim high, so that Singapore keeps moving forward, and our people continue to enjoy more opportunities and a better quality of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A crucial enabler for growth is our ability to attract high-quality and high-value investments to Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because such projects bring the latest know-how and capabilities, and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So far, our investment pipeline has been healthy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite a challenging external environment last year, the Economic Development Board (EDB) exceeded its targets, and brought in investments which are expected to create over 20,000 new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the competition for investments is getting tougher.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Governments around the world are rolling out vast subsidies to attract investments, especially in strategic industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, in November last year, Japan announced that it would allocate ¥2 trillion, or about $18 billion, to support its semiconductor industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot afford to engage in a “bidding war” with the major economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Essentially, this new tax credit will help us to stay competitive and attract investments from global companies with the right know-how and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides anchoring new investments, we must build on our existing strengths and upgrade the sectors where we have competitive advantages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These advantages did not come about by chance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are the result of many decades of hard work to restructure and upgrade our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also enhanced our capabilities and moved up the value chain, so as to justify the higher premiums for operating out of Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we are pressing on with these restructuring efforts through the Industry Transformation Maps.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we have many things going for us – our excellent connectivity, our reliability and stable business environment, and also a critical mass of leading companies based here, and they operate across the value chain, from design, to wafer fabrication, to assembly and testing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The companies here do not produce cutting-edge 3 nm chips, which you will read about in the media these days.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they have carved out a niche in other types of chips, like specialty chips and NAND flash memory chips.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are critical enablers of automation, 5G and electric vehicles, and they are in high demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how our little red dot can be a key node in the semi-conductor supply chain – accounting for more than 10% of the global semi-conductor market and 20% of semi-conductor equipment in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise in finance, we are a leading centre in Asia, supporting businesses from all over the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And during this period of global uncertainty, we have been able to distinguish ourselves as a stable and trusted financial centre.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The major financial institutions are keen to do more out of Singapore and we are seeing a continued inflow of investments, capital and talent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, whether in advanced manufacturing or high-end services, the strengths we have today are not easily replicated by others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the global competitive landscape is ever-changing and other countries, you can be sure, are seeking to overtake us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) more resources to take full advantage of current opportunities, and extend our lead in the financial services sector – not just to do more in the core areas of banking, capital markets, asset management, and insurance, but also to build capabilities in new areas like fintech, as well as green and transition finance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will set aside more funds for research and development (R&D), because this is how we push the frontiers of innovation across the entire economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will sustain our investments in research, innovation, and enterprise at about 1% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional resources will go towards research and related investments in national priorities such as advanced manufacturing, sustainability, the digital economy and healthcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our investments in R&D will take some time to translate into concrete economic outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this is precisely why we must take a long-term view.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For these investments help to develop a critical mass of capabilities, ideas and talent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They enable us to sharpen our competitive edge globally, as a knowledge-based and innovation-driven economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides a steady commitment to R&D, we also need to harness the full power of technology across our key sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One critical emerging technology is artificial intelligence (AI).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: AI is not just about ChatGPT or Large Language Models.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a general-purpose technology, like electricity, the internal combustion engine, the computer, or the internet.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It has the potential to transform a wide range of industries, and to enhance productivity across many existing processes, from drug discovery, to organising warehouses, or driving vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore is already recognised as a serious player in AI development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We aim to go further – to build new peaks of excellence, and crowd in private sector resources along the way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have set out the plans to do so in the National AI Strategy 2.0.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Part of the investment will be used to ensure that Singapore can secure access to the advanced chips that are so crucial to AI development and deployment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also work with leading companies in Singapore and around the world to set up their AI Centres of Excellence here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want these Centres to spur industry collaboration and innovation, and drive greater value creation across the whole economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In tandem, I will allocate additional resources to catalyse investments in upgrading our Nationwide Broadband Network.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This also ensures that our connectivity infrastructure will be able to support technologies like AI and immersive media, as they become more pervasive in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to do more to invest in and strengthen our local enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are helping smaller firms harness technology through pre-approved solutions, many tailored for the needs of specific industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This enables the small and medium enterprise (SMEs) to “plug and play” and quickly achieve greater efficiency and productivity gains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As companies grow, their needs will become more complex, especially as they go overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are providing more customised support to help these companies scale up, and we will continue with these efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One way for our companies to level up quickly is to partner with the multinational enterprises (MNEs) that are based here in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The MNEs set high requirements and standards for firms that wish to supply to them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot force MNEs to choose only local suppliers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we can and we will help Singapore enterprises to meet the high standards, and to form win-win partnerships with the MNEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Aerospace parts must meet stringent manufacturing and safety requirements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, aerospace manufacturers like Rolls-Royce, are highly selective in who they choose as partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Zincode, a local company was supported by the Smart Manufacturing Joint Lab – this is a collaboration between A*STAR, Rolls-Royce and Singapore Aero Engine Services Private Limited.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The company was supported by this lab to improve its image processing capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, it qualified as one of the approved partners for inspection work at the Rolls-Royce manufacturing facility here in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Zincode has now successfully captured new opportunities from other companies in the aerospace sector and benefited from an increase in sales.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to help more companies like Zincode raise their capabilities and win new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we have the Partnerships for Capability Transformation (PACT) scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the enhanced PACT, we aim to help more of our firms plug into global supply chains, compete in markets abroad and grow to become industry leaders in their own right.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For firms to be competitive, they also need to embrace sustainability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: SMEs today sometimes still treat sustainability as an additional imposition and cost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But going green can be a competitive advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because the MNEs are already looking to reduce their carbon footprint and they expect their suppliers to do the same.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also enhance the Energy Efficiency Grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond pre-approved energy-efficient solutions supported under the Grant, we will provide additional support for companies with more ambitious plans to reduce their emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry will elaborate on this and other sustainability-related measures at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are taking concrete steps to keep our economy competitive and vibrant, and to help our enterprises seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do whatever it takes to secure our place as one of the leading economic hubs in the world, known for our innovation, dynamism and deep capabilities, with good jobs and opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are investing heavily in our human capital, including in preschool and education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But learning cannot stop when formal schooling ends.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we launched SkillsFuture – to systematically support Singaporeans in reskilling and upskilling, and equip them throughout life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Singapore workforce today ranks highly in terms of skills and technical proficiency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our workers are able to command a premium in the global marketplace because of their expertise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with rapid technological advances, expertise is in constant flux.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Jobs like data entry clerks and door-to-door salesmen have dwindled in numbers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: New jobs that did not exist decades ago, like data scientists and digital marketers are now in demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, robots and machines will not completely replace humans at work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they will change the way expertise is defined and how value is created.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We therefore have to invest even more in our human capital, and help our workers refresh and update their skills, and learn how to harness new technologies more effectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, this is something that the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and the Labour Movement have consistently championed, most recently in the Forward Singapore engagements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also built up a wide array of training options, which individuals enjoy generous subsidies for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have made good progress over the past decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is still much more to be done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Continuous skills upgrading throughout life is now more important than ever.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must firmly establish SkillsFuture as a key pillar of our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Quality learning and skills training is not just about attending a one- or two-day course.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Workers may need weeks or months of training to get a proper skills reboot, especially if they are looking to move to a different area of work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even if they stay in the same industry, they will need a substantial injection of skills from time to time to stay relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will share the broad thrusts of this package or programme, and the Minister for Education will provide more details at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All Singaporeans aged 40 and above will get the top-up in May this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For those who are younger, you do not have to worry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Your turn will come – you will get the top-up, when you turn 40.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have deliberately allowed the existing basic tier of $500 in SkillsFuture Credit to be used for a wide range of courses, and this was to instil a habit of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The new $4,000 credit will be more targeted in scope – we will confine its usage to selected training programmes with better employability outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes part-time and full-time diploma, post-diploma, and undergraduate programmes, as well as courses for the Progressive Wage Model sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want participants taking up these programmes to be assured of better employment outcomes after they have completed their training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, we will give every Singaporean another bite of the education subsidy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even after you have graduated from an Institute of Higher Learning as a younger person, you can come back again after you turn 40 to do a full-time diploma and it will be at subsidised rates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every individual can receive up to 24 months of such a training allowance throughout their lifetime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will support the full duration of a SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme and more than half the duration of most qualifications issued by our Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What do these changes mean for our workers?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take the example of Mr Calvin Li, 40 years old now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He graduated from Singapore Polytechnic with a Diploma in Electronic, Computer and Communication Engineering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He works today as a Project Director at Khoon Engineering, which is a mechanical and electrical service provider.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, Calvin will enjoy a $4,000 top-up in SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He can use the Credit to pursue a second diploma.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This diploma will be offered at subsidised fees and the Credit will cover more than half of the expense after subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Should he intend to do this full-time, he can receive the monthly training allowance of up to 50% of his previous pay for two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will reap the full benefits only if all of us – Government, employers, workers, and unions – lean forward to truly deepen this culture of lifelong learning and skills mastery in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This must be our shared commitment to one another – to help our fellow Singaporeans develop to their fullest potential and to have productive and meaningful careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is one other move we will make under SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that technological changes will bring about more churn in the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even when the economy as a whole is doing well, some businesses or even some industries may be suffering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, it is not possible to have an economy that is dynamic and growing without failures and losses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In some sectors, firms will have to let go of people, while in other sectors, new and better jobs will be created.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it does not mean we should be indifferent to the suffering caused when firms lay off their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Losing a job is a major setback for workers and their families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who become involuntarily unemployed naturally feel the pressure to rush into the first available job they find.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the new job may not always be a good fit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ideally, they should consider ways to upgrade their skills and to find a job that fits their aptitude and talent.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But displaced workers may not have the time to train or search for new jobs, especially when they are already straining to make ends meet.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Therefore, we will do more to support this group of workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to design this scheme carefully, including the quantum of support and the conditionalities that come with the support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is to avoid the pitfalls other countries experienced when they introduced unemployment benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are working out the parameters for the scheme, and will provide more details later this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ours must always be an economy that provides opportunities for all; an economy that benefits the many rather than the few.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are making significant enhancements to SkillsFuture, and supporting jobseekers while they search for their next opportunity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We believe that every worker matters; that every citizen counts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will equip every Singaporean to benefit from the fruits of our economic growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In many developed countries, rising inequality and slowing social mobility have fractured social cohesion and deeply divided their peoples.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, we embarked on the Forward Singapore exercise because we do not want to succumb to the kind of harsh inequality we see in so many parts of the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By creating more paths towards equality and mobility, we also put ourselves in a better position for continued growth – in other words, a strong economy and a strong society reinforce each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But tackling inequality is often easier said than done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ideas on how to do so are frequently replete with unintended consequences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Simple handouts and blunt measures do not solve poverty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why Singapore has continually paved our own way since the beginning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We carefully study the experiences of others, taking note of where they have succeeded and failed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduce significant innovations that work for us, for our ethos, for our society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the last decade, we have made progress in uplifting lower-wage workers, and reducing disparities in wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our income inequality, as measured by the Gini coefficient, has declined to its lowest level over two decades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Workfare and Progressive Wages are our key strategies to uplift our lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will make several adjustments to ensure they continue to deliver results.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This ensures that we continue to cover lower-wage workers, even as their wages grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I will raise the Local Qualifying Salary (LQS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All local employees at companies that hire foreign workers must be paid the LQS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This increase ensures we keep pace with wage growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, I will provide more support for employers who raise the wages of their lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2022, I introduced the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS), where the Government co-funds the wage increases of lower-wage workers with employers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know employers are concerned with rising business costs in today’s economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also raise the PWCS wage ceiling from $2,500 to $3,000 in 2025, in tandem with the increase in the qualifying income cap for Workfare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To provide for these enhancements, I will top up the PWCS Fund by $1 billion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides uplifting lower-wage workers, we also want to improve wages across different professions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There will always be differences in wages in any society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But too large a gap creates unhealthy levels of anxiety and stress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Parents and children may get caught up in an education arms race, or may feel pressured to prioritise careers only in a few traditional fields, instead of focusing on their individual strengths and talents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, the vast majority of Singaporeans in the Forward Singapore engagements welcome broader definitions of success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want more diverse pathways so that every individual can strive to be the best possible version of themselves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This also means that we must accord greater value to those who are skilled in technical hands-on abilities, as well as those with the social and empathetic traits to excel in service jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, the wages and career prospects of our ITE graduates should not be too far below their polytechnic- and university-going peers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I was inspired by their personal stories, and their enthusiasm to deepen the skills they have acquired at ITE.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One of them, Matthew Francis Thanarajoo, graduated from ITE in 2021 with a Higher Nitec in Mechatronics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He is now pursuing a Diploma in Mechatronics at Temasek Polytechnic and honing his skills in automation and robotics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These experiences have equipped him with confidence to pursue his aspirations in engineering.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He will be representing Singapore at the WorldSkills competition later this year in France and we wish him the very best.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to encourage and support more young ITE graduates in their upskilling efforts, so they can excel in a profession they have trained in, and get themselves onto a better career and wage trajectory.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will therefore provide more support for ITE graduates aged 30 and below through a new ITE Progression Award.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, I will provide a $5,000 top-up to the Post-Secondary Education Accounts of ITE graduates when they enrol in a diploma programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help to offset the costs of obtaining a diploma.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give them a head-start in purchasing a home or saving for retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It represents our continuing commitment to uplift them, and to better equip them in their journey of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides tackling inequality, we must also uphold social mobility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Up to now, Singapore has fared better than other advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must continue to pay special attention to children from less well-off families, to ensure they have access to full and fair opportunities early in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of these families are already taking steps to build better lives for themselves, but they may find it hard to sustain progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that they often face complex challenges, including marital stress, existing debts, or even motivation and self-confidence issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under the enhanced ComLink (ComLink+), we are providing more customised support for these families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are getting family coaches and volunteer befrienders to work directly with these families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will jointly develop action plans to improve their life circumstances, and the coaches will provide additional support to the families, so as to encourage and motivate them towards these goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional support will be rolled out in the form of ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is yet another major innovation in our social policy landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those who make voluntary contributions to their CPF will receive matching grants from the Government to grow their savings faster.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This, combined with existing schemes like the Fresh Start Housing Scheme, will help these families buy their own homes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also partner with corporates and community groups to implement the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The donors can provide additional financial support to these families, and contribute in other ways, like befriending and mentoring, to help them get back on their feet again.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is how we keep the Singapore Dream alive and well for all our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I want to emphasise that this is not just about the Government doing more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also need our employers, community groups, as well as families and individuals themselves, to step up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together, we can and we will build – a fairer, a more equal, and a more inclusive Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, let me touch on our plans to build a Singapore made for families – an endearing home for all of us to sink roots, grow up and grow old in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Families are the bedrock of our society, and we will support their needs at every stage of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to take steps to improve preschool affordability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At Government-supported preschools, we extend generous subsidies, so that out-of-pocket expenses are kept affordable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is before the childcare subsidies which all families will benefit from.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will make another move to reduce fee caps in 2026.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also enhance existing preschool subsidies for lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In schools, we will do more to help our children develop the competencies and values they need to thrive in a more unpredictable future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is placing more emphasis on competencies like adaptive and inventive thinking, communication skills and civic literacy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For young couples who are getting ready to settle down and form their own families, timely access to affordable housing is critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are helping first-timer families by ramping up Build-To-Order (BTO) supply and giving these families greater priority.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also making flats in choicer locations more affordable, in a way that is fair and inclusive, through the Prime, Plus and Standard framework.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be implemented later this year for new BTO projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some couples have already booked their BTO flats, but they may like to have a place to stay temporarily, while they wait for the completion of their flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is especially the case for those with young children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, HDB offers subsidised rental housing under the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: HDB receives many applications for the scheme, and it is ramping up supply to meet the demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, I will do more for families of persons with special needs or disabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know that families of children with special needs face greater cost pressures due to higher fees for education and care services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each student at a Special Education (SPED) school already benefits from more subsidies than a primary school student in a mainstream school.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the fees at most SPED schools remain higher than those of mainstream schools due to the higher underlying costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are studying further moves to alleviate the cost pressures on these families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also lower the fee caps at all Special Student Care Centres to reduce families’ out-of-pocket expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For adults with disabilities, I will provide more support for their employment and integration into the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will expand spaces in Sheltered Workshops and Day Activity Centres where they can undergo skills training and launch more Enabling Services Hubs to provide community support to persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The respective Ministers will share more on each of these moves at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will do more to support the retirement needs of our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also provide the CPF Transition Offset to employers for another year, to cover half of the increase in employer contributions for 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help to cushion the impact on business costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I will raise the Enhanced Retirement Sum (ERS) from 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will allow more members aged 55 and above to fully commit their accumulated CPF savings to receive higher CPF payouts, should they wish to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will take steps to rationalise the CPF system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, members aged 55 and above have a Special Account (SA) and a Retirement Account (RA).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From next year, we will close the SA for those aged 55 and above.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The SA savings will be transferred to the RA up to the Full Retirement Sum, where they will continue to earn the long-term interest rate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The remaining SA savings will be transferred to the Ordinary Account (OA).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But members can voluntarily transfer their OA savings to the RA at any time, up to the ERS, to earn higher interest, and to receive higher retirement payouts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also enhance the retirement support schemes for seniors who need more help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Matched Retirement Savings Scheme (MRSS) helps Singaporeans aged 55 to 75 with less CPF savings to save more, by providing dollar-for-dollar matching for cash top-ups to their CPF accounts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will make several adjustments to the scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will extend the MRSS to those above the age of 70.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will enable more Singaporeans to meet their retirement needs, with help from their families, employers and the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will increase the annual matching cap from $600 to $2,000, and set a lifetime matching cap of $20,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, we provide a tax relief to encourage Singaporeans to top up their CPF.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the matching grant is already a significant benefit extended by the Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will remove the tax relief for the cash top-ups that attract the matching grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These changes to Silver Support and the MRSS will take effect from 2025. “Young Seniors” who currently in their 50s and early 60s will get an additional boost for their retirement through the Majulah Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was announced by Prime Minister Lee at last year’s National Day Rally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While the package is geared towards supporting Young Seniors, Pioneer and Merdeka Generation seniors will benefit too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, all Singaporeans born in 1973 or earlier will receive at least one component of the Majulah Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, I will provide an Earn and Save Bonus, to help seniors earning up to $6,000 per month accumulate more retirement savings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They will receive a yearly bonus of up to $1,000 for as long as they work, with more going to those who earn lower incomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, I will provide a one-time Retirement Savings Bonus of between $1,000 and $1,500 to seniors with retirement savings below the Basic Retirement Sum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Both bonuses will be for seniors who live in a property with Annual Value of $25,000 or less, and own no more than one property.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, I will provide a one-time MediSave Bonus to all seniors born in 1973 or earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Young Seniors with less means will be given the higher tier of $1,500; and all other seniors will receive $750.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more details at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To honour this commitment without burdening future generations, I will set aside $7.5 billion in a new Fund – the Majulah Package Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be sufficient to cover the lifetime cost of the Package, after accounting for investment income of the Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, we have invested heavily to ensure healthcare remains affordable and accessible for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have put this spending to good use.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are devoting more resources to areas of growing importance, like preventive health, support for our seniors and mental health and well-being, as recently affirmed by this House.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also continue to enjoy improvements in health outcomes, with Singaporeans living longer and healthier lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But with a rapidly ageing population, the fiscal pressures of healthcare will only grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a responsible Government, we have to plan ahead and set aside sufficient resources to keep healthcare affordable for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because if we wait, we will end up imposing a heavier burden on our future selves and our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, individuals also have a part to play.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we launched Healthier SG to empower all Singaporeans to take charge of our own health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While it is still early days, the momentum is encouraging.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One of them is Mdm Rubiah, who turns 69 this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: She credits her Healthier SG consultation for timely advice on how best to manage her health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, she is monitoring her blood pressure daily, cutting down on ice cream and "keropok" in her diet, and staying active through exercise classes and nature walks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And she has also helped to spread the word, by volunteering at a Healthier SG roadshow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Heed your doctor’s advice, participate in programmes that help you stay healthy and even pass it on by contributing as a senior volunteer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even with healthier lifestyles, all of us will still need some form of medical care as we get older and especially nearer to the end of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must expect healthcare costs, including medical insurance premiums, to rise, even after generous Government subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will benefit about 1.4 million Singaporeans and help them to cover their smaller medical bills and insurance premiums.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Coupled with the Majulah Package for older cohorts, we will collectively provide a MediSave Bonus for about three million Singaporeans this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To provide more support for healthcare costs, I will also update the per capita household income thresholds for our healthcare and associated social support subsidy schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Such schemes include MediShield Life premium subsidies, Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) subsidies for primary care, and subsidies for outpatient and inpatient treatments at our public hospitals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes to the per capita household income thresholds will mean additional Government spending in healthcare and other related areas of around $300 million per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: More than one million Singaporeans can expect to benefit from higher subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will provide greater assurance for healthcare costs, which will also reduce the financial pressures on caregivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Loneliness can do great harm to a senior.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They need to stay active and socially connected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, an expanded network of Active Ageing Centres, so that all seniors can look forward to a wider range of programmes at these centres, from physical exercises to volunteering opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, for seniors with care needs, we will develop more assisted living options, such as Community Care Apartments and better home care arrangements, to empower them to age confidently in their homes and community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, “silver upgrades” to our residential estates, to enable seniors to live more independently and safely in the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will cover amenities like therapeutic gardens and barrier-free ramps, and senior-friendly home fittings like wider toilet entrances and shower seats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fourth, improvements to our commuter infrastructure for seniors’ mobility and safety.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This means more sheltered linkways, bus stops with senior-friendly features, as well as safer and more pedestrian-friendly roads.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through these investments, we will provide more assurance to all Singaporeans – to set minds at ease, improve lives and well-being and ensure Singapore remains home truly for all of us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Alongside our investments to strengthen our economy and society, we will also make the investments needed to forge a stronger and more united nation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will safeguard what makes Singapore special and resilient – our commitment to take care of and defend one another, sustain the trust we have in each other and our institutions and build our strong sense of national pride and identity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since Independence, we have invested steadily to safeguard our peace and security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the last two decades, we have allocated around 3% to 4% of our GDP annually to the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF)’s budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, over the past decade, our spending on domestic security has doubled to more than $8 billion, or about 1.3% of our GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to build and maintain a strong and effective Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and Home Team.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will invest in them, and upgrade their capabilities year by year, to protect ourselves from potential aggressors and security threats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The backbone of our defence and security remains National Service (NS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope this will go some way in expressing our appreciation and gratitude to our national servicemen as well as their families for all that they have done and continue to do for our country.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In today’s world, defence and security apply not just in the physical environment, but also in the digital domain.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Scams, ransomware, data breaches, denial of service and other cyber threats have become increasingly commonplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The development and adoption of new technologies like AI and quantum computing will also change the threat landscape.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Cyber attacks will increase in speed, scale and sophistication.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have taken steps to strengthen our cyber defence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will improve our capabilities to monitor, detect, and coordinate our defences against cyber threats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides the conventional areas of security, we need to address an emerging security challenge – and that is energy, but more specifically, the transition to cleaner energy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the near to medium term, natural gas, which currently generates almost all of our electricity, will remain critical.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Natural gas is the cleanest of all fossil fuels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will not be able to achieve net zero emissions if we continue to rely solely on natural gas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, we do not have many options for clean energy – we have no tidal power, no wind power and not enough land for the mass deployment of solar.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is a limit to importing electricity without compromising security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will need other options to decarbonise the rest of our energy supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are actively exploring other options.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hydrogen has the potential as a clean fuel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For now, it is still technologically nascent, costly, and risky.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nevertheless, we have set out a National Hydrogen Strategy to take purposeful steps forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will start by testing and deploying ammonia, which is a hydrogen carrier, for power generation and bunkering on Jurong Island.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are actively studying the possibilities for geothermal power.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After all, we do have a hot spring in Sembawang.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this will require deep drilling to assess the potential, and it really remains to be seen if this will be viable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Further out in the future, we do not rule out nuclear power.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nuclear technologies are advancing rapidly, with smaller, safer and more fuel-efficient designs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will build up our capabilities, so that we can critically assess the evolving technologies in this space and decide on the feasibility of nuclear deployment one day in the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is considerable uncertainty as to how all these energy pathways will work out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What is clear, however, is that significant effort and costs will be needed to transit from a system powered almost entirely by natural gas today, to one powered largely by clean energy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We say this is an “energy transition”. “Transition” sounds like a rather innocuous word.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the scale of this so-called transition is massive, and we will need to get it done over the next two decades or so, which is not a lot of time, when you think about the enormity of the task.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, to import low-carbon electricity, we will need to invest in submarine cables and upgrade our existing power grid.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Or if we decide to scale up the use of hydrogen, we will need to put in place new infrastructure for generation, storage and delivery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The resilience of our nation is not only measured by what we spend, or by our infrastructure and hardware.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Rather, our true resilience lies within – in the strong bonds Singaporeans have forged among ourselves and in our collective willingness to take care of each other.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
