text: Every Singaporean man, woman, and child knows he or she belongs to this island nation, everyone has a place in our society, and each has a role to play in our unfolding Singapore story.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the essence of Total Defence, which we commemorated for the 40th time yesterday.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We nurture these bonds between Singaporeans by strengthening our culture of giving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are many who have done well in Singapore and want to give back, but may not know how or where to start.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will do more to help donors better appreciate the needs of our society and advise them on how to more effectively direct their resources – financial or non-financial – to support lower-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This effort will be led by the Community Foundation of Singapore, in partnership with the Ministry for Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Community Chest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will support collaborative projects among charities to enhance their governance, efficiency and capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Singaporeans readily step forward to support those affected by humanitarian crises overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We saw this in the relief efforts following the devastating earthquake in Türkiye and Syria last year; and also in the generous donations in response to the human tragedy arising from the Israel-Hamas conflict.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will run for four years as a pilot scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A stronger culture of giving will bind us closer together and make us a more caring and gracious society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another way to strengthen our solidarity is through the common experiences that we all partake in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The arts and sports provide us with the platforms to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The arts help to express our unique Singaporean culture, strengthen our shared bonds and make Singapore a distinctive home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of this plan, we aim to make the arts more accessible to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will unlock more opportunities and touchpoints for our artists to infuse the arts everywhere in our city and our communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional investments will also strengthen the foundation for a more vibrant arts industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: NAC will support arts groups to develop and showcase their diverse arts offerings as well as strengthen the talent pool.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Self-employed artists will also benefit from more development opportunities to broaden and deepen their skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Apart from the arts, there are few endeavours that can rally the country and ignite the Singapore spirit like sports.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From the grassroots to the global stage, from community participation to high performance, sports bring Singaporeans from all walks of life together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the grassroots level, we will enable more Singaporeans to participate in sports by continuing to support the Sports Facilities Master Plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With this, Singaporeans can look forward to new and rejuvenated sports centres in Toa Payoh, Punggol and Clementi, as well as more sports and recreational facilities in our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Singaporeans want to support our national athletes and we will provide them with more platforms for them to do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will anchor more major sports events in Singapore, so that our athletes can compete in top-tier competitions against the world’s best on home ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will allow more Singaporeans to cheer for Team Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In addition, I will broaden the scope of donations eligible for matching to cover athletes in emerging sports, like pickleball, tchoukball and powerlifting.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also include SportCares, which provides opportunities for vulnerable children and youth, persons with disabilities and seniors to participate in sporting programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will share more about our arts and sports initiatives at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Economic growth or social transfers alone cannot guarantee that we succeed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This Budget therefore invests in our national resilience – from ensuring the effectiveness of our military and domestic security, to safeguarding our energy security and building a stronger national identity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will shield us from external threats and the forces that threaten to pull us apart.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Only then can we be confident that Singapore will endure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our ability to invest in our economy, our society and our resilience has to be anchored on a strong fiscal position.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Fiscal responsibility has always been a key part of the Singapore DNA.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We spend our resources wisely, and we take care to provide for our children and grandchildren.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why I made major revenue moves in the last two Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be capped at $200 so that the benefits go mostly to our middle-income workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The rebate will cost the Government $350 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, taxpayers may claim a range of dependant-related reliefs, if their dependants have an annual income of $4,000 or less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In Budget 2022, I announced a two-step increase in Property Tax rates for residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was meant as a wealth tax, targeted at all investment properties, as well as the higher-end segment of owner-occupied properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Prior to that Budget announcement, market rents had been relatively flat for the preceding five years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But from 2022 onwards, market rents increased significantly due to the combination of strong demand and COVID-related supply constraints.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, the Annual Values (AVs) also increased sharply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had originally expected the Property Tax changes to impact mainly the top 7% of owner-occupied residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The AV increases resulted in the proportion of affected owner-occupied properties nearly doubling to 13%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will still uphold the intent of the Property Tax changes and ensure that those residing in higher-value properties continue to pay their fair share of taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government had provided a rebate to cushion the impact of the Property Tax changes this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to closely monitor the property market and will provide another rebate in 2025 if needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recognise that there are retirees living in higher-end residential homes, who face cash flow issues when paying their Property Tax bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To help them, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) will offer a 24-month instalment plan without any interest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They can apply for this via IRAS’ website or contact IRAS for more details.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, I will adjust the Additional Buyer’s Stamp Duty (ABSD) for the purchase of residential properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, married couples with an existing residential property can enjoy an ABSD refund on their replacement private property under the ABSD concession for Singaporean married couples.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, these seniors will be able to claim a refund of ABSD paid on their replacement private property, if they sell their first property within six months after purchasing a lower-value replacement private property.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also introduce some flexibility to the ABSD regime for housing developers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Housing developers are now granted an ABSD remission, provided they sell all the units in their development within a prescribed sale timeline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But despite their best efforts, the developers sometimes face difficulties in meeting this timeline requirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This ensures that housing supply continues to be released promptly, while providing some flexibility to the developers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The details of this change will be released in a statement later today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, on Corporate Income Tax – I will make significant adjustments to our tax system to take into consideration the international Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) 2.0 initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Pillar 1 aims to reallocate taxing rights on profits to market jurisdictions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When implemented, it will result in revenue losses for Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Pillar 1 has been delayed for now, and the implementation date remains unclear.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Pillar 2 will introduce a global minimum effective tax rate of 15% for large MNE groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last Budget, I announced our intention to implement Pillar 2 from 2025 and that we would monitor and adjust the timeline if needed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The European Union, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Japan and Korea are implementing Pillar 2 rules from 2024.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others, like Hong Kong and Malaysia, have announced their plans to do so from 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore move ahead with two components of Pillar 2, as planned.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The first is the Income Inclusion Rule (IIR).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A jurisdiction that introduces this will subject the overseas profits of MNE groups parented in that jurisdiction to a minimum effective tax rate of 15%.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, MNE groups that are parented in Singapore will have to pay a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on their groups’ overseas profits, regardless of where they operate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The second component is the Domestic Top-up Tax (DTT).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This applies to the Singapore profits of MNE groups operating here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Without this tax, these MNE groups would have had to pay their parent jurisdictions the effective tax rate of 15% on their Singapore profits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Therefore, it is in our interest to implement the DTT, so that we collect the tax, rather than have it go somewhere else.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will consider this at a later stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the DTT and IIR, we are already making major changes to our corporate tax regime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will focus on implementing these changes first, and ensure a smooth rollout for the affected companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the short term, the implementation of Pillar 2 will provide additional revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it is uncertain how much this will be and how long it will last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may even see a reduction in our tax base, should MNEs shift some of their activities to other jurisdictions in response to the new business environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In any case, whatever additional revenues we obtain from Pillar 2 will need to be reinvested for Singapore to stay competitive in a post-BEPS world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MNEs are now re-evaluating their plans and strategies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Other governments are also enhancing and refreshing their investment promotion toolkits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are introducing the Refundable Investment Credit, which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also have to spend more to support new investments, research and innovation activities, and to sustain our economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will also make some further tax adjustments, to ensure our tax system remains fair and competitive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Details of the tax changes are in the Annex to the Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These showed that Government spending has been rising steadily over the years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our spending in the late 2000s was around 15% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the span of ten years, it has grown by three percentage points of GDP, to around 18% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We expect spending to continue rising in this decade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Healthcare is one key driver for the increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are additional spending needs, fuelling the increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to spend more for the major moves to decarbonise our economy, as I explained earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of Forward Singapore, we are making significant policy shifts to strengthen our social safety nets and provide more assurance to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Assuming we stay within this range of spending increase, we should have sufficient revenues to maintain a balanced budget over the coming years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because there are so many pressures for us to spend more, be it on healthcare, social needs, or the energy transition, and these are all big-ticket items.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will have to manage these expenditures carefully, or we will end up with a significant funding gap.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We can already see this happening in many other advanced economies where public finances are on an unsustainable path, and the fiscal systems are at risk of breaking.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must never allow this to happen in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, let us uphold the ethos of fiscal discipline and responsibility that has served us well, and ensure that our fiscal position always remains balanced, sound and sustainable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For FY2023, our revenue collections were better than expected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This was mainly due to higher Corporate Income Tax collections.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The additional revenue will allow us to pay for new spending, including the $7.5 billion injection to the Majulah Package Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The overall stance is appropriate, as we are providing targeted support for households and businesses, even as the economy is projected to operate at around potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are living in a world which will become more violent, more fragmented, and more unpredictable in the years to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will try our best, working with others in the international community, to shape better global outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Great catastrophes often seem unthinkable until they happen.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Things may well get worse before they get better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must be mentally prepared and take steps now to adapt to this messy world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not the first time that we’ve found ourselves in such a situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since our Independence, we have had to adjust to all sorts of external disruptions and shocks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The British deciding to withdraw troops from Singapore in 1967; the global oil crises in 1973 and 1979; the Asian Financial Crisis in 1997; the dot-com bust in the early 2000s; 9/11; SARS; the Global Financial Crisis of 2008; and of course, more recently the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each time, we were able to weather the storms and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I believe we can do so again in our road ahead – so long as we stay united, work together, and continue to keep faith in one another.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Budget 2024 is about acting on this belief.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are helping Singaporeans with their cost-of-living concerns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are taking major steps to advance our Forward Singapore agenda.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For growth is the pre-requisite to create better jobs and raise living standards for all.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not the only country adapting to a different world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are the critical ingredients behind the Singapore story.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What we have today is rare, remarkable and unique.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: During the dark days of COVID-19, which feels like a bad dream to all of us now, I visited Riverside Secondary School.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The teacher had asked the students to imagine what they would be doing in 10 years’ time and to write a letter to their future selves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One student – Levin Ong – wrote, and I quote: “Dear future Levin, I hope you have been well in these past ten years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am grateful for how Singapore is dealing with COVID-19… the challenges I face are small compared to others during this difficult time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I want the world to be a better place and contribute back to society to the best of my ability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope, by 2030, I have made a better world for everyone.” Hope for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each one of us doing our best to make this a better place for all.
